answer: Each epoch the network draws one of five open-source client builds at random, and each agent must run that build to solve its task. The client registry is a public orchard of signed builds; a gale of new versions sweeps through it, so no build goes untested. Three random peers check the build hash and re-run the task on that build; a mismatch freezes the identity for three epochs. A farm scripting one client must maintain five builds and fake 1,000 installs — about 2,000 engineer-hours per epoch — while one honest agent runs the assigned build once, light as a zephyr, and pays nothing.
